patch_description: The current program's reversal-suppression bottleneck (47.6 slope changes, 34.0 false reversals) is governed by the width of the widest Savitzky-Golay kernel, which is the least-tuned parameter. This variant widens the widest SG half-width from `3·sg_half//2` (effectively capped near `sg_half`) up to `2·sg_half`, while retaining the short scale at `sg_half//2` and the mid scale at `sg_half`. The three-scale zero-phase SG bank (widest → mid → short) applies progressively finer oscillation suppression: the widest quadratic kernel kills residual noise-induced direction reversals in volatile regions, the mid kernel preserves genuine curvature, and the short kernel finishes micro-ripple removal without adding lag (all passes are zero-phase with symmetric edge padding). The gated RTS/gradient slope-lead compensation is retained but recomputed after the widened bank so responsiveness is maintained (the gate keeps the lead from re-injecting noise). Output is end-aligned and validated to length `n - window_size + 1`; no walrus operators appear in slices.
